title: Cyclone Murasu crosses Andhra coast near Ongole, uprooting trees and power poles
dek: The severe cyclonic storm crossed the coast between 3.30 am and 5.30 am and is set to weaken by noon; no deaths had been reported by 8 am, but crops, boats and power lines were damaged in Bapatla and Prakasam.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast close to Ongole between 3.30 am and 5.30 am on Tuesday, 3 November, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said, according to PTI and ETV Bharat. Winds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, uprooted thousands of trees, damaged hundreds of electricity poles and wrecked fishing boats, with extensive damage to standing crops reported in Bapatla and Prakasam districts, PTI reported.

The storm is expected to weaken into a cyclonic storm by noon on Tuesday and into a deep depression by midnight as it moves north over land, the IMD said. No deaths or injuries had been reported by about 8 am, The Week said, though officials had not yet released figures for damage, power cuts or people in relief camps. Heavy rain is expected to continue across south coastal Andhra Pradesh for the next 12 hours.

## Landfall

The landfall process began at 1 am, the IMD said. At 5.46 am it said the eye of the storm was entering the coast near Ongole with heavy rain and very strong winds at Kothapatnam beach, and that a major part of the wall cloud had moved over land, ANI reported. K. Nagaratna, director of the IMD's Andhra Pradesh centre, said red warnings were in force for Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, NTR and Prakasam districts, with offshore and onshore operations suspended and fishermen told not to go to sea until Wednesday morning, according to the Daily Jagran.

In Kothapatnam, a fishing village in Prakasam, a resident told PTI that the government had evacuated about 400 families from the village and that this was the most dangerous cyclone she had seen in 14 years. Trees fell in the Chirala area soon after landfall began, and vehicles were stranded on national highways because of poor visibility, PTI and the Daily Jagran reported.

South Coast Railway cancelled nine trains as a precaution, including the Vijayawada-Gudur and Gudur-Vijayawada expresses, and schools, colleges and anganwadi centres were shut in several districts of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Odisha, the Daily Jagran reported. In NTR district, collector Lakshmisha said families in Vijayawada's Mogalrajapuram had been moved to relief camps as a precaution against landslides, and that there were no major problems in the district so far, according to the same report.

## Rain and the state response

In Vijayawada, about 200 km north of the landfall point, heavy rain that began late on Monday night continued into Tuesday, waterlogging Bandar Road, Polyclinic Road and parts of One Town, ANI reported at 6.17 am. The outer rain bands also brought continuous rain to Puducherry from midnight, The News Mill reported. The IMD said heavy spells of rain were likely along the south Andhra coast over the next 12 hours, and it was tracking the storm with Doppler radars at Chennai and Machilipatnam.

At a teleconference in the early hours, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu told officials to stay on high alert and make sure there was no loss of life, saying deaths like those during Cyclone Arnab last week should not be repeated, according to ANI and The News Mill. He said winds were expected to be weaker than during Arnab, asked the power department to restore electricity immediately wherever it failed, and ordered steps to prevent breaches in canals and irrigation tanks. Officials told him heavy rain was forecast in 125 mandals.

## Andhra Pradesh prepares

Before landfall Naidu was told that 31,000 electricity poles had been sent to the field and 1,000 power-restoration workers were arriving from Chennai, IANS reported, and about 6,800 irrigation tanks in six districts were at risk of breaching. At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled on Monday at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam, PTI reported. The National Disaster Response Force had 13 of its 37 deployed teams in Andhra Pradesh, according to ANI.

The disaster management authority's helplines are 112, 1070 and 1800 425 0101, and the state's Mana Mitra WhatsApp helpline is 9552300009.

## What it means for Bengal

IMD Kolkata's latest bulletin, issued at 9 pm on Monday, says there is "No weather warning for West Bengal in association with this system", which it is monitoring continuously. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 has now been hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia ports, up from the Distant Cautionary Signal No. 1 hoisted on Saturday, with sectional signals II and IV at Sagar Island.

Light to moderate rain is likely at one or two places on Tuesday in Kolkata and several south Bengal districts, with dry weather across the state from Wednesday to 9 November, the bulletin said. There is no fishing warning for the Bengal coast.

## Odisha braces again

Southern Odisha is still recovering from Cyclone Arnab. IMD Bhubaneswar has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rain in Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam on 3 and 4 November, Argus reported. By Monday night more than 1.6 lakh people had been moved to safety across southern Odisha, against a plan to evacuate 3.33 lakh, the state government said, according to Deccan Chronicle.

## What happens next

With the storm now over land, the IMD expects it to weaken to a cyclonic storm by noon and a deep depression by midnight. Many districts will feel the heaviest rain on Tuesday, after the storm has crossed the coast, and Telangana is under a warning for isolated extremely heavy rain on Tuesday. The state government's first figures for damage, power cuts, crop losses and people in relief camps are expected later on Tuesday.

## Key numbers

- Landfall: process began at 1 am IST on 3 November; storm crossed the coast close to Ongole, Prakasam district, between 3.30 am and 5.30 am (IMD)
- Casualties: none reported by about 8 am (The Week)
- Transport: 9 trains cancelled (South Coast Railway); at least 19 flights cancelled on Monday
- Peak forecast wind: 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph
- Storm surge: 1-1.5 m above astronomical tide in the IMD's landfall release (1.5-2 m in earlier bulletins), highest over Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam
- Evacuated: Andhra Pradesh about 2,000 by Monday, with 30,000 more planned (state officials); Odisha more than 1.6 lakh (state government, via Deccan Chronicle)
- Red warning districts on Tuesday: Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, NTR, Prakasam (IMD Andhra Pradesh centre)
- Bengal: no warning; Distant Warning Signal No. 2 at Kolkata and Haldia ports
